I left a bug in `_reports`: the group index mapping. In `_apply_groups` the group list is:
`[attempt, role, signatures(dict), bad, closed, timeouts]` → indices 0..5: group[0]=attempt, group[1]=role, group[2]=signatures dict, group[3]=bad, group[4]=closed, group[5]=timeouts.

In `_reports` I wrote:
```
bad, closed, timeouts, signatures = group[2], group[3], group[4], group[5]
```
That's wrong ordering. Let me fix by unpacking correctly:
```
signatures = group[2]; bad = group[3]; closed = group[4]; timeouts = group[5]
total = bad + closed + timeouts + sum(signatures.values())
```
And remove the stray `total = len(signatures) + 0` and `total_rows` helper.

Also `_discovery` has an unused `order` parameter — fine, or remove.

Let me fix `_reports`.

    """Fold group decisions into per lease/service role subsets."""
    reports = {}
    for (lease, target, service), group in groups.items():
        report = reports.get(lease)
        if report is None:
            report = reports[lease] = {name: [set(), set(), set(), set(), 0]
                                       for name in service_order}
        entry = report[service]
        signatures, bad, closed, timeouts = group[2], group[3], group[4], group[5]
        total = bad + closed + timeouts + sum(signatures.values())
        entry[4] += bad
        if closed == total:
            status = 1                      # every latest row is closed
        elif bad or timeouts or closed or len(signatures) != 1:
            status = -1                     # unknown service state
        else:
            status = 0                      # one agreed open signature
        if status < 0:
            continue
        index = 0 if group[1] == ROLE_INTERNAL else 2
        entry[index + status].add(target)
    return reports


'''
p.write_text(t[:start]+new+t[end:])
